title: Monks Who Were Knights
bigQuestion: How did a small group of knights guarding pilgrims grow into one of the richest groups in Europe?

story.title: A Receipt for the Road
story.kicker: A traveler in France is scared to carry his money on a long trip. The knights next door have an idea.
paragraphs: It is a cold spring morning in France, about 850 years ago. A farmer we will call Pierre is packing for a long trip. He wants to walk to Jerusalem, a holy city far away. The trip may take many months. Pierre has saved coins for years to pay for food and boats on the way.

Pierre is worried. Robbers wait on the roads. A bag of coins is easy to steal. His neighbor tells him about the knights at the big stone house near the market. They wear white cloaks with red crosses. People say they keep money safe for travelers.

Pierre knocks on the heavy door. A brother in a plain cloak lets him in. Pierre sets his coins on a wooden table. The brother counts them slowly. Then he dips a feather pen in ink. He writes how much Pierre left on a small piece of parchment. He hands Pierre the written receipt.

Pierre folds the receipt and tucks it inside his shirt. Now he carries a piece of writing, not a heavy bag of gold. He walks out into the street feeling lighter. Pierre is a made-up person. But the knights and their money-keeping were real. Historians still study the records of how they did it.
story.think: Why might Pierre feel safer carrying a piece of paper than a bag of coins? What would he need to trust?

lessons.title: Pilgrims to Jerusalem
lessons.mainIdea: In the 1100s, many Christians walked to Jerusalem as pilgrims, and the roads there were dangerous.
reading: Jerusalem is a very old city. It is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims. In 1099, Christian armies from Europe took the city in a war. These wars are called the *Crusades*. After that, more Christian travelers came from Europe to visit.
A *pilgrim* is a person who travels to a holy place to pray. Many pilgrims landed at a port by the sea. Then they walked inland to Jerusalem. The road ran through dry hills with few towns.
Robbers hid along these roads. They attacked travelers and took their things. Pilgrims had no one to protect them. Some people began to ask: who will keep the travelers safe?

words.d: a person who travels to a holy place to pray
wars in which armies from Europe fought to control Jerusalem and nearby lands, starting in 1096

look.title: A Road in Words
look.text: Picture a dusty road climbing through brown hills. The sun is hot. A small group of pilgrims walks slowly. One leads a donkey with bags. There are no houses in sight. Behind a big rock, someone is watching them.
look.prompt: What dangers do you see on this road? What would help these travelers feel safe?

check.q: What is a pilgrim?
choices: A soldier who guards a castle
A person who writes history books
A person who travels to a holy place to pray
check.why: The reading says a pilgrim travels to a holy place to pray.

check.q: Why were the roads to Jerusalem dangerous?
choices: The roads were covered in snow
Boats could not reach the city
check.why: The reading says robbers hid along the roads and attacked travelers.

check.q: Jerusalem is holy to which groups?
check.why: The reading says Jerusalem is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims.

lessons.title: Hugh of Payns Starts a Brotherhood
lessons.mainIdea: About 1119 or 1120, a French knight named Hugh of Payns and a few friends promised to guard pilgrims.
reading: Hugh of Payns was a knight from France. About 1119 or 1120, he and a few other knights made a plan in Jerusalem. They would guard pilgrims on the roads. They would also live like monks, with prayer and simple lives.

They called themselves the Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ. King Baldwin II of Jerusalem gave them rooms in part of his palace. The palace stood on the Temple Mount. People then believed King Solomon's Temple had once stood there.

Because of that building, people called the knights the Templars. A *Templar* is a member of this order. An *order* is a group of people who live by the same religious rules. Their full name grew long: the Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon.

words.d: a member of the Knights Templar, a religious order of knights begun about 1120
a group of people who live by the same religious rules and promises

look.title: How It Began
rows: Hugh of Payns and friends begin (about)
look.cite: Malcolm Barber, The New Knighthood: A History of the Order of the Temple (Cambridge University Press, 1994)
look.prompt: How many years after the Christians took Jerusalem did the Templars begin? Show how you figured it out.

check.q: Who was Hugh of Payns?
choices: A French knight who helped start the Templars
A robber on the pilgrim road
check.why: The reading says Hugh of Payns was a French knight who began the brotherhood with a few friends.

check.q: Why were the knights called Templars?
choices: They built a temple in France
They lived on the Temple Mount, where people thought Solomon's Temple had stood
check.why: The king gave them rooms on the Temple Mount, so people called them Templars.

check.q: What is an order?
choices: A group of people who live by the same religious rules
check.why: An order is a group of people who live by the same religious rules and promises.

lessons.title: Two Dates for One Beginning
lessons.mainIdea: An old writer said the Templars began in 1118, but most historians today think it was 1119 or 1120.
reading: William of Tyre was an archbishop who lived in the Holy Land. In the 1170s and 1180s, he wrote a long history of the kingdom of Jerusalem. He told how the Templars began. He said it happened in 1118.

But William wrote about 50 years after the start. He was not there. Historians today compare his book with other old records. Most of them think the Templars began in 1119 or early 1120. The start is *documented*, but the exact year is *disputed*.
William also said there were only nine knights for nine years. Other records show Hugh traveling in Europe to find new members by 1127. So many historians think the nine-knights story is too simple.

words.d: shown by records or objects from the time
argued about; experts do not all agree
a church leader in charge of other bishops in a region

look.title: William of Tyre Tells the Story
look.text: In the year 1118, some noble knights, loyal to God, promised to live in poverty and obey the church leader of Jerusalem. The king gave them a home in his palace near the Temple. For nine years they wore only clothes that people gave them.
look.cite: William of Tyre, History of Deeds Done Beyond the Sea, Book 12, chapter 7 (written c. 1170s-1180s)
look.prompt: William wrote about 50 years after 1118. Which part of his story would you want to check against other records? Why?

check.q: What year did William of Tyre give for the Templars' start?
check.why: William of Tyre wrote that the Templars began in 1118.

check.q: Why do historians question William's date?
choices: He never wrote about the Templars
He wrote about 50 years later and was not there
check.why: William wrote about 50 years after the start, so historians check him against other records.

check.q: What does disputed mean?
check.why: Disputed means experts argue about it and do not all agree.

lessons.title: A Rule to Live By
lessons.mainIdea: In about 1129, church leaders at Troyes, France, gave the Templars a written Rule of 72 parts.
reading: In about 1129, church leaders met in the town of Troyes, in France. Hugh of Payns came to ask for their help. The meeting is called the Council of Troyes. There, the Templars got a written *Rule*.

A Rule is a book of rules for how members of an order live. The Templars' first Rule was written in Latin. It had 72 short parts. Much of it was based on an older Rule for monks, the Rule of Saint Benedict.
A *monk* is a man who gives his life to God and lives by strict rules with other monks. Most monks prayed and worked quietly. The Templars were new. They were monks who also rode to battle.

words.d: a written set of rules for how members of a religious order live
a man who gives his life to God and lives by strict rules with other monks

look.title: A Rule Book You Know
look.text: Think of the rules posted in your classroom. One says to raise your hand. One says to walk in the hall. One says to put supplies back. Each rule helps the whole class work together. Now imagine a rule book with 72 rules for every part of your day.
look.prompt: Pick one classroom rule. What problem does it solve? What problem might a rule about meals or clothing solve for a group of knights?

check.q: Where did the Templars get their first written Rule?
choices: At the Council of Troyes in France
check.why: Church leaders at the Council of Troyes, in France, gave the Templars their Rule in about 1129.

check.q: How many parts did the first Templar Rule have?
check.why: The first Rule, written in Latin, had 72 short parts.

check.q: What made the Templars different from most monks?
choices: They were monks who also rode to battle
check.why: Most monks prayed and worked quietly. The Templars were monks who also fought.

lessons.title: Three Promises and Quiet Meals
lessons.mainIdea: Templars promised to own nothing of their own, not to marry, and to obey their leaders.
reading: When a man joined the Templars, he made three big promises. He would own nothing for himself. He would not marry. He would obey the leaders of the order. Promises like these are called vows. Each one is a *vow*.
The Rule filled each day with prayer. The brothers ate meals together in one hall. They were to eat quietly while someone read aloud. Their clothes were plain, with no fancy decorations.

Some rules were about knightly life. The Rule said how brothers should care for their horses. It also said the brothers must not go hunting for fun. The one animal they were allowed to hunt was the lion.

words.d: a serious promise, often made to God
a member of a religious order of men

look.title: From the Templar Rule
look.text: The brothers should eat together and keep quiet at the table while a holy book is read. Their clothes should be plain, with nothing just for show. They should not hunt birds or other animals for sport. Only the lion may be hunted.
look.cite: The Latin Rule of the Templars, Council of Troyes, c. 1129; English translation in J. M. Upton-Ward, The Rule of the Templars (Boydell, 1992)
look.prompt: Pick one rule. What do you think it was meant to teach the brothers about how to live?

check.q: What is a vow?
check.why: A vow is a serious promise, often made to God.

check.q: Which was one of the three Templar promises?
choices: To obey the leaders of the order
To live alone in the woods
check.why: Templars promised to own nothing, not to marry, and to obey their leaders.

check.q: Which animal did the Rule allow the brothers to hunt?
check.why: The Rule said the brothers must not hunt for fun, but the lion was allowed.

lessons.title: White Mantle, Red Cross
lessons.mainIdea: Templar knights wore a white mantle, later with a red cross, so everyone could see who they were.
reading: A *mantle* is a long cloak worn over other clothes. The Rule said the knights should wear white mantles. White stood for a clean, pure life. Other brothers wore black or brown.
In the 1140s, a pope allowed the Templars to add a red cross to their clothes. The red cross showed they would give their lives for their faith. Soon the white mantle with the red cross was famous.

The Templars also had a *seal*. A seal is a stamp pressed into wax to show who sent a letter. Their seal showed two knights riding on one horse. Many people think it stood for being poor and sharing. Historians still talk about its meaning.

words.d: a long, loose cloak worn over other clothes
a stamp pressed into wax to show who sent a letter
a picture or sign that stands for an idea

look.title: Two Knights, One Horse
look.text: Look closely at a round wax seal. In the middle, two knights sit on one horse. Both hold shields. Both hold long spears. The horse is walking forward. Words in Latin run around the edge of the circle.
look.prompt: Why might a group choose this picture as its symbol? Give one idea about what it could mean.

check.q: What is a mantle?
choices: A long cloak worn over other clothes
check.why: A mantle is a long, loose cloak worn over other clothes.

check.q: What color mantle did Templar knights wear?
check.why: The Rule said knights wore white mantles. Other brothers wore black or brown.

check.q: What did the Templar seal show?
check.why: The Templar seal showed two knights on one horse.

lessons.title: Gifts of Land
lessons.mainIdea: People across Europe gave the Templars land and money, so the order grew rich and set up houses in many countries.
reading: Many people in Europe admired the Templars. They wanted to help guard the pilgrims. So they gave gifts. Kings and nobles gave land, farms, mills and money. Some farmers gave a small field.

The Templars set up houses on this land. A Templar house that ran farms and land in one area is often called a *commandery*. Soon there were Templar houses in France, England, Spain, Portugal, Italy and other lands.
Most brothers in Europe were not fighters. Many ran farms. They sold crops and wool. They sent money and horses east to the knights in the Holy Land. The farms in Europe fed the fight far away.

words.d: a Templar house that ran farms and land in one area
a person from a rich, powerful family, often with land and a title

look.title: A Map in Words
look.text: Picture a map of Europe. Put a small dot for each Templar house. Dots fill France. Dots spread into England, Spain and Portugal. More dots appear in Italy and farther east. Now draw arrows from all the dots to one place: Jerusalem.
look.prompt: What do the arrows show? How did houses far from Jerusalem help the knights there?

check.q: Why did people give land to the Templars?
choices: The Templars bought all of it
The king made them sell it
They wanted to move to Jerusalem
They admired them and wanted to help guard pilgrims
check.why: The reading says people admired the Templars and wanted to help, so they gave gifts.

check.q: What is a commandery?
choices: A Templar house that ran farms and land in one area
check.why: A commandery was a Templar house that ran farms and land in one area.

check.q: What did most Templar brothers in Europe do?
choices: Ran farms and sent help east
check.why: Most brothers in Europe ran farms and sent money and horses to the Holy Land.

lessons.title: Keeping Money Safe
lessons.mainIdea: The Templars kept money safe and moved payments from place to place, an early kind of banking.
reading: The Templars had strong houses and trusted brothers. So people asked them to keep money safe. A person could leave coins or treasure at a Templar house. This is called a *deposit*. The Templars kept a record of it.

The Templars also helped move money over long distances. Their houses were in many countries. They could write down a payment in one place and settle it through another house. Historians call this a *transfer*. It is safer than carrying gold on a ship.

In time, even kings trusted them. The Templar house in Paris kept money for the kings of France. Historians call this an early kind of *banking*. Some popular books add more details. Historians are careful to say only what the old records show.

words.d: money or treasure left with someone to keep safe
moving money from one place or person to another
the work of keeping, lending and moving money for people

look.title: Coins or a Note?
look.text: Two travelers leave the same town. The first carries a heavy bag of coins. It clinks with every step. The second carries a folded note that says how much money she left at a Templar house. It fits in her sleeve.
look.prompt: Which traveler would a robber notice first? What must the second traveler trust for her plan to work?

check.q: What is a deposit?
choices: Money left with someone to keep safe
check.why: A deposit is money or treasure left with someone to keep safe.

check.q: Whose money did the Templar house in Paris keep?
check.why: The reading says the Paris Templar house kept money for the kings of France.

check.q: Why could the Templars move money over long distances?
choices: They had houses in many countries
check.why: Their houses in many countries let them settle a payment through another house.

lessons.title: Castles and Round Churches
lessons.mainIdea: The Templars built strong castles in the Holy Land and in Europe, and churches in many towns.
reading: In the Holy Land, the Templars guarded roads and borders. They built and held castles. One, near the sea at Atlit, was begun about 1218. It was called the Pilgrims' Castle. Its thick walls faced the water on three sides.
In Portugal, the Templars built a castle at Tomar, begun in 1160. It became their main house in that country. Its round church still stands today. Visitors can walk inside it.

In London, the Templars built the Temple Church. Its round part was blessed in 1185. Part of it is round. It was built to remind people of a famous round church in Jerusalem. You can still visit it. A *castle* guarded land. A church was for prayer. The Templars needed both.

words.d: a large, strong building with thick walls, built to protect people and land
the area around Jerusalem, holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims

look.title: Templar Buildings That Still Stand
look.cite: Helen Nicholson, The Knights Templar: A New History (Sutton, 2001)
look.prompt: Which building is the oldest? About how many years apart are the oldest and the newest?

check.q: What was the Templar castle at Atlit called?
check.why: The castle begun at Atlit about 1218 was called the Pilgrims' Castle.

check.q: Which Templar building is in London?
check.why: The Temple Church in London was blessed in 1185.

check.q: Why is part of the Temple Church round?
choices: To remind people of a round church in Jerusalem
check.why: The reading says it was built round to remind people of a famous round church in Jerusalem.

lessons.title: A Famous Monk Cheers Them On
lessons.mainIdea: Bernard of Clairvaux, a famous monk, wrote a letter praising the Templars as a new kind of knight.
reading: Bernard of Clairvaux was one of the most famous monks in Europe. People listened when he spoke. Hugh of Payns asked him for help. Around the 1130s, Bernard wrote to Hugh and his knights. His writing is called In Praise of the New Knighthood.

Bernard said the Templars were a new kind of knight. Ordinary knights often fought for money or pride. Bernard said Templars fought to protect others and lived simple, holy lives. He praised their plain clothes and their obedience.

Bernard's letter was a kind of *praise*. It helped the Templars find new members and gifts. When you read old writing, it helps to ask who wrote it and why. Bernard wanted people to support the new order. He was their *supporter*.

words.d: words that say good things about someone
a person who helps a group and speaks up for it

look.title: Bernard's New Knight
look.text: Bernard wrote that this new knight fights two battles at the same time. One battle is against enemies he can see. The other is against evil inside the heart. He said such a knight has no fear, because he trusts God.
look.cite: Bernard of Clairvaux, In Praise of the New Knighthood (De laude novae militiae), c. 1130s
look.prompt: Bernard was a supporter of the Templars. How might that change the way he described them?

check.q: Who was Bernard of Clairvaux?
choices: A famous monk who praised the Templars
check.why: Bernard was one of the most famous monks in Europe. He wrote in praise of the Templars.

check.q: What did Bernard say made the Templars a new kind of knight?
choices: They fought to protect others and lived simple, holy lives
check.why: Bernard said they fought to protect others and lived simple, holy lives.

check.q: How did Bernard's letter help the Templars?
choices: It found them new members and gifts
check.why: The reading says Bernard's praise helped the Templars find new members and gifts.

lessons.title: A Critic Speaks Up
lessons.mainIdea: Some people, like William of Tyre, later said the Templars had grown too proud and too rich.
reading: Not everyone praised the Templars. As the order grew rich, some people grew uneasy. One of them was William of Tyre, the archbishop who wrote the history we read before.

William said the Templars began humble and poor. But he wrote that later they became proud. He complained that they did not obey the bishops of the Holy Land. The pope had let them answer to him alone, not to local bishops. That made some church leaders angry.

A *critic* is a person who points out what he thinks is wrong. Bernard was a supporter. William was a critic. To understand the Templars, historians read both. Each one saw part of the story from his own place.

words.d: a person who points out what he or she thinks is wrong
not proud; not thinking you are better than others

look.title: Two Writers, Side by Side
look.text: Writer A, Bernard (1130s): The Templars live plainly. They obey. They protect others. Writer B, William of Tyre (1170s-1180s): The Templars began humble. Now they are proud and rich. They do not obey the bishops here.
look.prompt: The two writers lived about 40 years apart. How could both be telling part of the truth?

check.q: What is a critic?
choices: A person who keeps money safe
A person who writes a Rule
A person who points out what he thinks is wrong
check.why: A critic is a person who points out what he or she thinks is wrong.

check.q: What did William of Tyre complain about?
choices: The Templars had grown proud and did not obey local bishops
check.why: William wrote that the Templars grew proud and did not obey the bishops of the Holy Land.

check.q: Why do historians read both Bernard and William?
choices: Each saw part of the story from his own place
Only one of them could read
check.why: Bernard was a supporter and William was a critic. Reading both gives a fuller picture.

review.q: What job did the first Templars promise to do?
choices: Guard pilgrims on the roads to Jerusalem
review.why: Hugh of Payns and his friends promised to guard pilgrims on the roads.

review.q: About when did the Templars begin?
review.why: Most historians think the Templars began in 1119 or early 1120.

review.q: The Templars were both monks and knights. What does that mean?
choices: They lived by religious rules and also fought
They sailed ships and sold wool
review.why: They made monks' promises and lived by a Rule, and they also rode to battle.

review.q: Which describes a Templar knight's clothes?
choices: A black robe with a gold star
A white mantle with a red cross
A red cloak with a white lion
review.why: Templar knights wore white mantles. In the 1140s they added a red cross.

review.q: How did the Templars become rich?
choices: People gave them land, farms and money
review.why: Kings, nobles and farmers gave the Templars land, farms, mills and money.

review.q: Which was an early kind of banking the Templars did?
choices: Keeping deposits safe and moving money between houses
review.why: The Templars kept deposits safe and helped transfer money over long distances.

review.q: How are Bernard of Clairvaux and William of Tyre different?
choices: Bernard was a critic and William was a supporter
Bernard praised the Templars and William criticized them
Neither one wrote about the Templars
review.why: Bernard praised the new knights. Later, William said they had grown proud and rich.

review.q: Which Templar building can you still visit in London?
choices: The palace on the Temple Mount
review.why: The Temple Church in London was blessed in 1185 and still stands.
